findings.title: Feature-flagged TableWidgetVisualization renders hardcoded empty data
findings.body: In `tableResultComponent`, when the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag is on, the new branch renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` instead of the real result. All of the actual widget data is discarded: `result.data`, `result.meta`, `eventView`, `fields`, `fieldAliases`, loading state, title, custom field renderers, and min column width are simply not passed. Any organization (or dogfooding/staff account) with that flag enabled will see completely empty dashboard/insights table widgets. The flag branch must either be wired to the real table data or not ship until it is; as written it silently breaks every table widget the moment the flag is flipped.

findings.title: fetch_error_details zips error_ids against nodestore dict values, misaligning ids with data
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`, and then pairs them with `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node id, and missing nodes are simply absent from the result, so `events.values()` is not guaranteed to be in the same order as `error_ids` and is shorter whenever any lookup misses. When one error event is missing (e.g. expired from nodestore), every subsequent pairing shifts, so an `ErrorEvent` gets the wrong `id`, `title`, `message`, and `timestamp`. Downstream, `gen_request_data` uses these timestamps to interleave error messages chronologically with replay breadcrumbs, so the Seer summary will report the wrong errors at the wrong times. The correct approach is to look up each id individually from the returned mapping (e.g. `data = events.get(node_id)`), not to zip two independently ordered sequences.

findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES are only filtered when a search query is active
findings.body: The new `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` filter for `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` is applied only inside the branch that runs when `searchQuery.trim()` is non-empty; the early `return sorted;` for an empty search bypasses it. That means these internal noise attributes are shown in the span attributes panel in the normal (no-search) case and only disappear once the user types a search — the opposite of what a constant named HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES implies. The filter should be applied to `sorted` before the empty-search early return.

findings.title: Analytics event recorded before the feature gate and request validation
findings.body: The `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` call was placed at the very top of `post`, before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check and before schema validation. As a result the event fires for every request, including ones that are rejected with 404 (feature disabled) and 400 (invalid payload), so the metric counts denied and malformed requests as assemble attempts and cannot be used to measure actual usage of the endpoint. Additionally, for org-auth-token requests `request.user` may not be a real user, so `user_id` can be `None` for a large share of recorded events. Record the event after the feature check (and ideally after the body validates) so the analytics reflect real assemble attempts.

findings.title: UseTraceItemAttributeBaseProps doc comment says only LOGS is supported, but SPANS is now used
findings.body: The doc comment on `UseTraceItemAttributeBaseProps.traceItemType` (moved into `explore/types.tsx` in this PR) states "The trace item type supported by the endpoint, currently only supports LOGS." However this same PR wires the hook family up for spans: `TransactionNameSearchBar` and `TraceItemSearchQueryBuilder` now pass `traceItemType: TraceItemDataset.SPANS` to `useGetTraceItemAttributeValues`/`useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys`. The comment is now wrong and will mislead future callers into avoiding the spans path.
